mathematical_definition: For each of the trailing 60 fully-resolved historical start points t0 (t0 in [i-window-sub_horizon, i-sub_horizon)), retrospectively checks whether |close[j]-close[t0]| >= 0.001*close[t0] (a 10bps move) was reached within the next sub_horizon=10 bars (j in (t0, t0+10]); hist_p_reach_10bps_10b_60 is the fraction of those 60 historical windows that reached the 10bps threshold (n_hits/n_checked) -- a LOCAL empirical first-passage probability, distinct from any global constant and from the barrier-touch labels themselves (numba kernel first_passage_stats, window=60, sub_horizon=10, r_threshold_frac=0.001)
numerical_stability_notes: n_checked is always 60 once past warmup (the outer window range always yields exactly `window` iterations), so the n_checked==0 guard is defensive only and not expected to trigger in steady state. Causality verified by direct code read during Phase 3 design (spec section 2): first_passage_stats's inner loop bound is t0 in [i-window-sub_horizon, i-sub_horizon) and j in (t0, t0+sub_horizon], so the maximum index ever read is j=i-1 -- every inner-loop index is strictly < i, no lookahead.
missing_value_policy: NaN for the first window+sub_horizon=70 bars, never zero-filled
